items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.summary:
A humanoid robot appears in a public place, playing with a child and attracting attention with its movements and interactions.

Short public demonstrations may look impressive on camera. However, the practical test remains how long the platform can operate autonomously, without a person nearby to adjust or restart it.

These videos demonstrate progress in movement and presence. It is the number of hours of reliable autonomous operation on real-world tasks that determines the device’s usefulness.

#AI #Robotics #HumanoidRobots #PhysicalAI #Automation #CuttingEdgeTechnology

items.title: This one actually made me pause.
items.summary:
This one actually made me pause.

Scientists built a robot made of liquid.
Not flexible.
Liquid.

It can split, merge, squeeze through tiny spaces, and then re-form.
When it breaks, it heals itself.

No motors.
No joints.
No rigid body.

I’ve spent years thinking about AI as the brain of machines.
This feels like the first glimpse of something else.

A body that does not have a fixed shape.

Today it’s millimeter-scale.
Tomorrow, it’s medicine moving through the body, or machines exploring places nothing solid can reach.

That thought excites me.
And honestly, it unsettles me too.

So here’s the question.
When machines no longer have a stable form, what does “control” even mean?

#AI #Robotics #SoftRobotics #Innovation #Technology #FutureOfWork

items.title: OPTIMUS DRIVES A TESLA FOR $43,000🚙
items.summary:
OPTIMUS DRIVES A TESLA FOR $43,000🚙

A humanoid robot sits behind the wheel of a Tesla, hands on the steering wheel, moving through real traffic.

No demo stage.

No controlled track.

Just a robot in the driver’s seat on public roads.

Most people still think humanoid robots are only good for factories and backflips.

This clip makes you wonder what happens when one of them can actually drive.

Is this the first real robot taxi… or just the beginning?

items.title: SHE NEEDS A FAN TO STAY COOL. THAT'S THE MOST REALISTIC PART OF THIS VIDEO. 🤖🌀
items.summary:
SHE NEEDS A FAN TO STAY COOL. THAT'S THE MOST REALISTIC PART OF THIS VIDEO. 🤖🌀

a robot expo. a crowd of phones. 
a girl with a glowing metal core where her waist should be. ✨
someone holds a little fan to it. she smiles, fixes her hair. 

the face? almost certainly AI. 
the fan? that's real robotics. 🔥
every motor, every battery, every AI chip makes heat. 🌡️
heat is one of the reasons real humanoids still work in short shifts and spend hours on chargers. 

so how far have robots actually come? 👇

📅 2015: at the DARPA challenge, robots fell over opening doors.
🤸 2025: humanoids do flips, box, and dance at expos.
📦 2025: Unitree shipped 5,500+ humanoids. AgiBot's CEO said 5,000+.
🇺🇸 Tesla, Figure and Agility: about 150 each (Omdia).
🏭 Hyundai plans a factory for 30,000 robots a year by 2028.

💰 Morgan Stanley: a $5 trillion humanoid market by 2050.
ten years from falling over to doing backflips. 
but the robots that exist are still grey, bulky and plugged in. 🔌

the "robot girl" is what the hype looks like.
the fan is what the engineering looks like. 🛠️
when the real ones catch up with this video, will you be able to tell the difference? 👀

items.title: Look at the sign behind her: "CROTTIE JON". "Toocenean".
items.summary:
Look at the sign behind her: "CROTTIE JON". "Toocenean".

That is not a company. That is AI spelling. The robot girl is a video prompt, not a product.

But the real robots got crazy cheap 👇

📉 THE PRICE OF A HUMANOID

2023 → Unitree H1: about $90,000
2024 → Unitree G1: about $16,000
2025 → Unitree R1: $5,900
2026 → R1 from about $4,300 in China, sold worldwide on AliExpress

From luxury car to used car in 3 years.

🏦 WHAT WALL STREET SAW

🔵 Goldman Sachs
In one year, the cost to build a humanoid fell about 40%. From $50K-$250K to $30K-$150K.
Goldman expected 15-20% a year.
Its 2035 market forecast jumped 6x: from $6B to $38B.

🟠 Morgan Stanley
More than 1 billion humanoids by 2050. A $5 trillion market.
Price per robot: from about $200K in 2024 to $50K in 2050.
About 90% of them for factories and shops, not homes.

🔴 The catch
The cheap R1 is 1.22 m tall, weighs 25 kg and runs about an hour per battery.
It is made for developers. It will not fold your laundry.
The robots that work in factories still cost tens of thousands.

💡 THE LESSON

A fake robot girl now costs one prompt.
A real robot costs less than a used car.

The video got perfect first. The robot is catching up on price.
Usefulness is the last thing left to fix.

items.title: NOBODY ASKS IF ROBOTS CAN WALK ANYMORE. THEY ASK WHAT A ROBOT CAN HOLD WHEN THE RECOIL HITS.
items.summary:
NOBODY ASKS IF ROBOTS CAN WALK ANYMORE. THEY ASK WHAT A ROBOT CAN HOLD WHEN THE RECOIL HITS.

Watch this humanoid plant its legs, take the burst and keep the barrel on target.

Recoil is one of the hardest balance tests for any body. Every shot hits the torso, the arms and the aim at once, and the control system has to answer in milliseconds.

A year ago the flex was a robot dancing. Now it is a firing line.

Video made in Sumi Studio.

The capability is here. The rulebook is not.
Who decides what a humanoid is allowed to hold?
The Sumi article breaks down the whole pipeline from node to final frame. Read the details in the quote below.
A little gift in the comments ↓↓↓

items.title: SHE LOOKS HUMAN. EVEN HER REACTIONS ARE STARTING TO FEEL REAL.
items.summary:
SHE LOOKS HUMAN. EVEN HER REACTIONS ARE STARTING TO FEEL REAL.

At a tech expo, a young woman approaches a humanoid robot and says, “I love your hair.”

The robot smiles, touches its hair, and responds to her.

People nearby stop to watch. Some pull out their phones. Others step closer to see how it reacts.

But look beneath its face.

Exposed wires, motors, and glowing electronic components reveal the machinery behind the human appearance.

The interesting part is how quickly humanoid robots are moving beyond basic movement and industrial tasks. They're now being designed to look human, express emotions, and interact naturally with people.

The technology still has a long way to go. But once robots combine realistic faces, natural movement, and convincing conversation, the potential market could be much bigger than people expect.

Some companies may end up selling more than robots.

They may be selling the feeling of interacting with another human.
